prompt: Put the five headings of Davi's page in the order they appear on it.
hint: The kernel first, then the two that make the page usable.
trap: Opening with how we will know turns the page back into a list of targets; the signals only mean something once the diagnosis and the choice are on the page.

prompt: What separates a strategy page from a proposal one-pager, by the lesson?
hint: How many times is each one consulted, and by whom?

choices.text: It is written for the CTO's approval
choices.why: That describes the proposal. The strategy page is written for the engineer deciding something next week, not for Helena, who already agreed.

choices.text: One asks for a single decision; the other serves many later ones
choices.why: Right: it is consulted again and again by people who were not in the room, about decisions it never mentions.

choices.text: It carries the full incident analysis behind the diagnosis
choices.why: The evidence is a link. The reader of the page needs the conclusion, and the reviewer of the evidence knows where to look.

choices.text: It runs longer, since it covers a year of work
choices.why: Both fit on one page. A strategy that runs long has usually not chosen yet.

prompt: Which of these belongs under "How we will know" on Coreto's page?
hint: A line there has to be able to come out false.

choices.text: Teams feel more confident about on-sales
choices.why: It cannot be false: somebody always feels better, whatever the on-sale did.

choices.text: The strategy page reaches every engineer by the end of March
choices.why: That is activity. It can go green while the on-sales keep failing.

choices.text: Each big on-sale ends with no seat-hold incident
choices.why: Right: it is an outcome tied to the diagnosis, and it is false the morning an on-sale fails.

choices.text: Reservations closes more tickets each sprint than the one before
choices.why: Tickets closed measure effort, not effect; the team could close more every sprint and the locks still hold.

prompt: Which of these go in the header of a strategy page, above the diagnosis? Choose all that apply.
hint: The page is going to be quoted in arguments.

choices.text: Who owns the page
choices.why: Right: a page that will be quoted needs somebody who answers for it and keeps it current.

choices.text: The incident analysis behind the diagnosis
choices.why: The evidence is linked from the diagnosis, not copied into the page.

choices.text: Who signed it
choices.why: Right: Helena's signature is what makes the page the company's position rather than Davi's opinion.

choices.text: When it will next be reviewed
choices.why: Right: a quotation needs a date, and the review is also when the repeat-back test is run again.

choices.text: Every team's original proposals, for the record
choices.why: That is the appendix the lesson starts by cutting; it is where the choice hides.

prompt: Your own strategy draft runs to three pages, and you have already cut the background. Where does the lesson tell you to look next?
hint: The cause is upstream of the writing.

choices.text: At the actions, which are written in too much detail
choices.why: Detail in the actions follows from the number of problems being addressed; trimming wording leaves the problems.

choices.text: At the layout: smaller type and two columns
choices.why: A page that fits by typography still asks the reader to absorb three strategies.

choices.text: At the not list, which belongs in a document of its own
choices.why: The not list is where the choice becomes visible; moving it out removes the part that does the most work.

choices.text: At the diagnosis: it covers more than one challenge
choices.why: Right: three problems produce three policies and a page of actions. Cut to the one that matters and the rest follows.

prompt: Why does the lesson put exclusions on the page by name, instead of letting the policy imply them?
hint: Think of the GraphQL gateway in lesson 2.

choices.text: It is kinder to the people whose projects were dropped
choices.why: Kindness is handled in the conversation before publication; the list exists for everybody else.

choices.text: An implicit exclusion is decided by each team, differently
choices.why: Right: without the line, a reasonable person could decide that one small service did no harm, and two teams did.

choices.text: Executives expect a strategy to show what it gave up
choices.why: The audience the lesson cares about is the teams making decisions, not the executives reading the page once.

choices.text: It keeps the policy short enough to fit in the title
choices.why: The policy is short either way; the list is about what the policy excludes, which a short sentence leaves unsaid.

prompt: Which of these lines passes the first test for the not list, that somebody reasonable wants it?
hint: A line earns its place by disappointing a real proposal.

choices.text: Neglect the reliability of checkout
choices.why: Nobody proposed neglecting it, so excluding it excludes nothing. It is fluff with a negation in front.

choices.text: Let quality slip to hit a date
choices.why: Nobody writes this down as a plan, so the line disappoints nobody and settles no argument.

choices.text: Stop listening to what venues ask for
choices.why: No team is proposing to ignore venues; a line against it is a value statement, not a choice.

choices.text: Move to a new front-end framework
choices.why: Right: Catalogue had volunteered to pilot it. The line costs a real team a real project, which is why it is worth writing.

prompt: Match each weak line for a not list to what is wrong with it.
hint: Three tests: somebody wants it, it names the thing, it says until when.

pairs.right: It forbids the strategy's own work
It gives no end, so it reads as permanent

right_distractors: It is too long for one page

prompt: By the lesson, nobody whose project is on the not list should first learn it from the ___.
hint: Davi talked to Rafaela and Mateus before publishing.

prompt: Davi's line forbids changing the reservation path in the on-sale season "for cost or for features, unless the change has passed the load test". Why not write "No changes to reservations" instead?

choices.text: Mateus would have refused to sign a page with a blanket ban
choices.why: Mateus signs nothing; Helena signs the page. The objection to the blanket line is in the strategy itself.

choices.text: Short lines are read as permanent and get argued with
choices.why: A missing end date is a real weakness, but adding "this year" would still forbid the Reservations team's job.

choices.text: It would forbid the work of action 3 itself
choices.why: Right: removing the row locks is a change to the reservation path. The real line excludes changes made for other reasons, in the dangerous season, without evidence.

choices.text: Product would read it as a freeze on every feature
choices.why: Product would read it correctly; that is not the trouble. The trouble is that the line contradicts action 3.

prompt: Why does the lesson call the third question, a case the page does not mention, the one that matters most?
hint: A person can memorise a sentence.

choices.text: It is the hardest, so it ranks the five people best
choices.why: The test does not rank people; it tests the page. A failed answer points at what to change on it.

choices.text: Applying the policy to a new case takes understanding
choices.why: Right: recitation passes the first two questions. Only somebody who understood the policy can apply it where the page is silent.

choices.text: It checks whether people read the page to the end
choices.why: The case is not on the page at all, so reading to the end would not help; understanding the policy would.

choices.text: The first two questions are about memory, and memory fades by the quarterly review
choices.why: Fading memory is why the test is run again each quarter, not why the third question matters most.

prompt: In Davi's second round, five people answered three questions each. How many of those fifteen answers passed?
hint: Add the totals under the three columns of the second grid.

prompt: The Payments engineer said: "We're moving off the monolith, slowly." Why does the lesson call it the most useful answer in the table?
hint: Who wrote that version of the strategy?

choices.text: It shows which engineer skipped the page
choices.why: The test is of the page and its delivery, not of the person; blaming her would hide the rumour.

choices.text: It proves the policy was the wrong one for Coreto
choices.why: A misremembered policy says nothing about whether the policy is right; the incident log decides that.

choices.text: It shows that the not list was too long to remember
choices.why: The list had four lines. Its position at the bottom of the page was the problem Davi fixed.

choices.text: A version nobody wrote is going round, and it will make decisions
choices.why: Right: no migration this year had become a slow migration, and that version will steer choices until it is corrected.

prompt: Helena tells Davi that most of the company opened the strategy document in its first week. What does that tell him?
hint: Opening is not reading, and reading is not remembering.

choices.text: That the strategy has landed and the test can wait
choices.why: Readership measures delivery of the message. The first round showed three of five could not say the policy back.

choices.text: That he should test only those who did not open it
choices.why: The people who opened it are exactly the ones the test is for; opening it does not show they can use it.

choices.text: Nothing about whether anybody can use it
choices.why: Right: a published, opened page can still be a page nobody carries in their head.

choices.text: That the page is short enough, since people opened it and read it in one sitting
choices.why: Nothing in an open count says how long anybody stayed or what they kept.

prompt: Put the steps of the repeat-back test in order.
hint: The page changes last, and only where the answers point.
items: Wait a week or two after publishing
Pick five people who did not write it, across teams
Ask the three questions without the page
Write down each answer in their words
Change the page or its delivery where answers fail
trap: Asking on the day of publication measures the first read, not what stayed; and changing the page before writing the answers down loses what told you what to fix.

prompt: Another company's policy is "Make the platform self-service". All five people asked say "self-service" back, word for word, and none can say whether a team may configure a database by hand for a launch. What has the test found?
hint: Which of the three questions failed?

choices.text: A pass: all five repeated the policy correctly
choices.why: Repeating the words passes the first question only; the new case is where understanding shows, and it failed.

choices.text: Recitation without understanding: the new case failed
choices.why: Right: the policy was memorised and cannot be applied, which points at a policy that rules out too little to decide the case.

choices.text: The engineers need training on the platform first
choices.why: Training on the tool would not tell them what the strategy allows; the gap is in the policy, not their skills.

choices.text: The not list is too long to hold in memory
choices.why: Nothing says the list is long; the answers show the policy was remembered and could not be used.

prompt: Which change did Davi make after the first round of the test?
hint: Everybody who sees a link to the page now reads the policy.

choices.text: He put the policy into the page's title
choices.why: Right: the title now reads "protect the on-sale first", so the policy is the first thing anyone sees.

choices.text: He added background so the reasons would be clearer
choices.why: Background is what the lesson cuts; the reasons were clear, and the policy was buried.

choices.text: He asked the same five people again, a week later
choices.why: He asked five different people a month later; the same five would have been answering his correction.

choices.text: He moved the not list to a separate page for the teams affected
choices.why: He moved it up, beside the actions, so that what the company does and does not do are read together.

prompt: Match each heading of Davi's page to a line that sits under it.
hint: One is a measure, one an exclusion, one an action.

pairs.right: The seat-hold code that every team changes and no team owns
Platform builds a load test that replays an on-sale
Rewrite the reservation module from scratch
Checkout availability on on-sale days reaches 99.99%

prompt: By the lesson, every line under "How we will know" should be able to come out ___.
